chapter: Kid Rene, Chris Kelly and the bungalow
title: Kid Rene at the Cadillac nightclub
summary: After leaving gambling work he returned to music with Kid Rene at the Cadillac, where Papa Kutcher begged him to stay.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Barney. Barney. We were talking about the band you played with. After Buddy Petit and Sidney Ted Fien. Did you ever play with Kid Rene? You said you did play with Kid Rene. How about how long did you play with?

Well, I played with Rene. I'll let you know. Just a minute. I played with Kid Rene at the Cadillac nightclub. I played until it closed. Is that down at St. Claude? St. Claude, right after the 5th precinct. Papa Kutch used to own it then. Had his brother join church and stopped playing then when you joined Kid Rene? Yeah, his brother joined church. And he had another drummer by the name of Nathan. So I gave up, stopped playing music for a while. I was making so much money in my line of work that I kept so busy that I forgot about music. So he came over to me and says, Come on, you want to work with me? I said, oh man, I ain't played music in no way. Yeah. What job were you doing then? I was in the gambling business. I was in the gambling business. I was making so much money. Like band, huh? Yeah. Band bourgeois? Yeah, I think $25, $30 a day. So I says, oh no. I said, oh, I say yeah. He said, come on. I said, man, I wouldn't even know how to make a roll. He said, oh man, once you learn something, you don't ever forget. I said, oh man, I can't come. So he's big with someone. So I went. I told my mom I'm going to work for a few nights with you. So finally, he's such a nice guy. I agreed to play with him. I put somebody in my place to work for a couple nights. So I've been so good down there that I told him, I said, well, Renan, I'm going to leave you this week. So I don't know what he went and told Papa Kutcher. He was calling old man Papa Kutcher to have the place. Papa Kutcher called me on the Friday night and said, what's the matter, Big Garden? I said, well, I'm leaving you all this week. He said, oh no. No, no. I said, yeah, I'm leaving you this week. He said, why? I said, yes, so. I said, I'm tired. He said, oh, put somebody in your place one night to dress up. I said, no, I'm tired. He said, oh no, you can't do that. He said, you can't quit. He said, I ain't going to let you quit. So, Renan, he was all uneasy. I said, well, he begged me to stay and Papa Kutcher begged me to stay. So we stood until Papa Kutcher then sold the place out. His brother took over the place. Then his brother got tired. Then he sold the place out. He told me he died. I know how true it is, Papa Kutcher. I never knew him. I didn't know him myself. But he was just going to let me quit. He just kept me there. He said, no, you ain't going nowhere. He said, you're going to stay right here. And everybody liked me down there. Everybody liked the mock man. So it was just one of those things. Renan was so glad to have me. So after the job closed down, I went to work at the Brown Diver. That's where you say you see him in. At the Brown Diver. Well, did you ever play with Chris Kelly? Chris Kelly? Yeah. I played with Chris Kelly about three, four years. I played with Chris Kelly.
